comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative physical cycling; pr-1953 cuts open a taped parcel, opens its flaps, and retrieves the contents.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key insertion, counterholding, fine collar rotation, torque-limited relocking, and response-based adjustment. pr-1953 requires guarded cutting, bimanual flap opening, tool return, and item transfer. Shared grasping and bimanual primitives do not constitute task overlap.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable physical stops within damper stroke and energy/velocity limits, with no bottoming, hard-stop strike, excessive rebound, overload, or lock drift. pr-1953 requires completing three tape cuts, returning the cutter, opening both flaps, and placing the item within 3,600 steps. Its body reports full-score demonstrations but provides no spec versions or detailed numeric fracture, damage, or placement thresholds.
comparison.reason: The records test meaningfully different abilities: dynamic damper tuning and retained mechanical adjustment versus safe package cutting, opening, and extraction. Different objectives, manipulation sequences, failure modes, and completion criteria establish distinction despite generic shared primitives.
